knowledge:
- key_parameters: snp.list=A list defining the genotype file path, format (e.g., "tped"), and subject list ;; pheno.list=A list defining the phenotype file path, ID variables, file type, delimiter, response variable, strata variable, main effects, and interaction variables ;; op=An options list for GxE.scan which can specify output file, model type, custom scan functions, setup functions, and genotype filtering options ;; strata.var=The stratification variable used for the constrained maximum likelihood (CML) method ;; cc.var=The variable containing matched set IDs for case-control matching in snp.matched ;; nn.var=The variable containing matched set IDs for neighbor matching in snp.matched
- alternatives: PLINK or GLU=External software that GxE.scan can call to automatically transform genotype data if they are installed on the system
- when_to_use: Appropriate for case-control genetic association studies where researchers want to test for gene-environment (GxE) or gene-gene (GxG) interactions, especially when leveraging gene-environment independence in the control population via CML or EB methods to increase statistical power.
- pitfalls: TPED files do not contain subject IDs, so a matching subject.list (like a TFAM file) must be provided to align genotypes with phenotypes ;; If a SNP has missing values during a custom scan, the base model must be refit on the non-missing subset to ensure valid likelihood ratio tests ;; Running GxE.scan on a single processor for an entire GWAS will take a long time; users should partition the scan for cluster computing using GxE.scan.partition and GxE.scan.combine.

workflows.name: gxe_scan_tped
workflows.intent: Run a genome-wide association scan for gene-environment interactions using TPED genotype files and a phenotype file.
input: pheno.txt (Tab-delimited phenotype file containing response, strata, and covariates)
workflows.stages: 1. Define the subject list from the TFAM file ;; 2. Define the snp.list with the genotype file and format ;; 3. Define the pheno.list with phenotype file details and model variables ;; 4. Set output options ;; 5. Run the GxE scan using GxE.scan ;; 6. Read and inspect the output file
workflows.code:
subject.list <- list(file=subject.file, id.var=1:2, header=0, delimiter=" ")
subject.list <- subject.file
snp.list <- list(file=geno.file, format="tped", subject.list=subject.list)
pheno.list <- list(file=pheno.file, id.var=c("Family", "Subject"),
              file.type=3, delimiter="\t",
              response.var="CaseControl", strata.var="Study",
              main.vars=c("Gender", "Exposure", "Smoke_CURRENT", "Smoke_FORMER"),
              int.vars="Exposure")
out.file <- paste(getwd(), "/GxE.out", sep="")
op <- list(out.file=out.file)
GxE.scan(snp.list, pheno.list, op=op)
x <- read.table(out.file, header=1, as.is=TRUE, sep="\t")
x[1:5, ]

workflows.name: snp_logistic_interaction
workflows.intent: Fit logistic regression models (UML, CML, and EB) to evaluate gene-environment interactions on a case-control dataset.
input: Xdata (Data frame containing case-control status, SNP genotypes, stratification variables, and covariates)
workflows.stages: 1. Create dummy variables for categorical covariates ;; 2. Fit the interaction model using snp.logistic ;; 3. Extract model summaries using getSummary ;; 4. Perform Wald tests for the SNP and interaction terms using getWaldTest
workflows.code:
for (a in unique(Xdata[, "age.group"])) {
  dummyVar <- paste("age.group_", a, sep="")
  Xdata[, dummyVar] <- 0
  temp <- Xdata[, "age.group"] == a
  if (any(temp)) Xdata[temp, dummyVar] <- 1
}
mainVars <- c("oral.years", "n.children", "age.group_1",
              "age.group_2", "age.group_3", "age.group_5")
fit <- snp.logistic(Xdata, "case.control", "BRCA.status",
                     main.vars=mainVars, 
                     int.vars=c("oral.years", "n.children"), 
                     strata.var="ethnic.group")
getSummary(fit)
getWaldTest(fit, c("BRCA.status", "BRCA.status:oral.years", "BRCA.status:n.children"))

workflows.name: matched_case_control
workflows.intent: Perform matched case-control analysis by creating matched sets and fitting conditional models.
input: Xdata (Data frame containing case-control status, SNP genotypes, matching covariates, and interaction variables)
workflows.stages: 1. Compute a distance matrix using daisy ;; 2. Generate matched sets using getMatchedSets ;; 3. Append matched strata to the dataset ;; 4. Fit matched models using snp.matched ;; 5. Summarize the CLR and CCL models using getSummary ;; 6. Perform Wald tests on the HCL model using getWaldTest
workflows.code:
library("cluster")
size <- ifelse(Xdata$ethnic.group == 3, 3, 4)
d <- daisy(Xdata[,c("age.group_1","gynSurgery.history","BRCA.history")])
mx <- getMatchedSets(d, CC=TRUE, NN=TRUE, ccs.var = Xdata$case.control, 
	  strata.var = Xdata$ethnic.group, size = size, fixed = TRUE)
Xdata <- cbind(Xdata, CCStrat = mx$CC, NNStrat = mx$NN)
intVars <- ~ oral.years + n.children
snpVars <- ~ BRCA.status
fit <- snp.matched(Xdata, "case.control", snp.vars=snpVars,
                     main.vars=intVars, int.vars=intVars, 
                     cc.var="CCStrat", nn.var="NNStrat") 
getSummary(fit, method = c("CLR", "CCL"))
getWaldTest(fit$HCL, c( "BRCA.status" , "BRCA.status:oral.years" , "BRCA.status:n.children"))
